nodes.summary: For a point $c = (a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, a radius $r > 0$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the lollipop with center $c$, radius $r$ and stem direction $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ consists of the circle $\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = r^2\}$ and the stem $\{c + s(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) : s \ge r\}$, the part of the ray from $c$ in that direction outside the open disc. For all…
nodes.title: Stem–circle intersections of two lollipops

nodes.summary: For a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the constrained long-legged T $\bar T(c, \theta)$ is the union of the crossbar, the line $\{c + s(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta) : s \in \mathbb{R}\}$, and the stem, the ray $\{c + s(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) : s \ge 0\}$. For all $c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and $\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \mathbb{R}$, if $\bar T(c_1, \theta_1) \cap \bar T(c_2, \theta_2)$…
nodes.title: Four-point intersections of constrained T's

nodes.summary: For a tip $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$, nonzero vectors $u_1, u_2 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and reals $a, b > 0$, the long-legged A is the union of the rays $\{c + s u_1 : s \ge 0\}$ and $\{c + s u_2 : s \ge 0\}$ and the crossbar segment $[c + a u_1, c + b u_2]$. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ long-legged A's can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for long-legged A's

nodes.summary: A long-legged three-armed V is the union of three rays $\{c + s u_j : s \ge 0\}$, $j = 1, 2, 3$, from a common tip $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$, with nonzero direction vectors $u_1, u_2, u_3 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ in arbitrary directions. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ long-legged three-armed V's can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for three-armed V's

nodes.summary: For points $p, q \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and nonzero vectors $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the 3-chain is the union of the ray $\{p + s u : s \ge 0\}$, the segment $[p, q]$ and the ray $\{q + s v : s \ge 0\}$; the directions are arbitrary and the 3-chain may intersect itself. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ 3-chains can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for 3-chains

nodes.summary: The empty set of cuts divides the plane into exactly one region.
nodes.title: No cuts, one region

nodes.summary: For a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of cuts, the number of regions into which $K$ divides the plane is the number of connected components of the complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$, or $0$ if there are infinitely many components.
nodes.title: Number of regions cut out of the plane

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
